x: In the 100 Yards Peter Vine won his heat in 11.7. but was unplaced in the second round. Later on he was unsuccessful in the 220 Yards.
Peter Vine was beaten by an American by inches in 9.7. Clay proved a winner in the Final, and completed the "double" by winning the furlong off 15 in 22s., Jim Harding being second a few inches away.

Grieve, of the School, once again won both sprints, although young Peter Vine was a good runner-up in both races, and this finely-built young man should prove a good addition to our sprinting strength.
The 100 Yards, won in 10.1s., saw Peter Vine about a yard away with Hayes fourth. Peter stepped into the breach and tackled the quarter, and was a good third in 54.1.

If Arthur gets really fit, then who ever wishes to win the Macher Shield will have to go all the way. Peter Vine, having recovered from his injury sustained playing football about two years ago, is playing again—this time for Kingstonians.
Peter Vine, we hear, is in Palestine for a few months on business.
